Package com.nexuslink.protocol.mongo

Class MongoService

java.lang.Object
com.nexuslink.protocol.mongo.MongoService
All Implemented Interfaces:
AutoCloseable
public final class MongoService extends Object implements AutoCloseable
MongoDB client built on the official synchronous driver. Connect with a standard connection string (mongodb://host:port or mongodb+srv://…), then browse databases/collections and run find / aggregate / CRUD operations.

Blocking by design — callers run it off the UI thread. Filters and pipelines are supplied as MongoDB Extended-JSON strings and parsed with the driver's own parser.

    • findDetailed

      public MongoFindResult findDetailed(String collection, MongoQuerySpec spec)
      A find with the full Compass query bar: filter, projection, sort, skip and limit. Every part is Extended JSON and may be blank. Documents come back decoded as well as rendered, so the tree view can show real BSON types rather than re-parsing the JSON it just printed.

    • setField

      public long setField(String collection, Object id, String path, Object value)
      Sets one field of one document, by _id and dotted path, to an already-typed value — the save behind an in-place tree edit. Unlike replacing the document it touches nothing else, so a concurrent edit to another field is not silently reverted.
      Returns:
      the number of documents modified (0 when the value was already that)

    • runShell

      public MongoQueryResult runShell(String line)
      Runs one mongosh-style line — the shell tab. Parsing is MongoShellCommand's job; this method maps a parsed command onto the driver and renders whatever came back, so a read prints documents, a write prints its counts, and a line outside the grammar prints the reason rather than failing silently.

    • watchChanges

      public MongoService.ChangeWatch watchChanges(String collection, String pipelineJson, Consumer<ChangeEvent> onChange, Consumer<String> onError)
      Watches a collection (or the whole database when collection is blank) and reports each change as it happens — the change-streams panel.

      Change streams need an oplog, so they only exist on a replica set or a sharded cluster; a standalone is refused up front with that explanation rather than a driver error. The returned handle stops the watch and closes the cursor.

      Parameters:
      onChange - called on the watching thread for every change event
      onError - called once if the stream ends unexpectedly

    • previewPipeline

      public List<StagePreview> previewPipeline(String collection, String pipelineJson, int sampleSize)
      Runs an aggregation pipeline one stage at a time, reporting after each what survived: the document count, how it moved, and a sample of the output.

      Each stage costs two cheap queries (a $count and a $limited sample) rather than materialising the pipeline, and a stage that fails stops the walk — everything after it would fail the same way, and the first error is the one worth reading.

    • exportCollection

      public long exportCollection(String collection, String filterJson, CollectionTransfer.Format format, Path file, int headerSample, LongConsumer progress) throws IOException
      Exports a whole collection to a file, streaming rather than loading it into memory: documents are written as they arrive from the cursor, so a collection larger than the heap still exports.

      CSV needs a header before the first row, so the column set is taken from a bounded sample first (headerSample documents) — otherwise it could only be known after reading everything. Fields outside that sample are not exported to CSV; JSON has no such limit.

      Parameters:
      progress - called with the running document count, for a progress bar
      Returns:
      the number of documents written
      Throws:
      IOException

    • importDocuments

      public long importDocuments(String collection, List<org.bson.Document> documents, int batchSize, LongConsumer progress)
      Inserts documents in batches, reporting progress as it goes. Batching is what makes an import of any size finish in reasonable time; the batch is deliberately unordered so one bad document does not stop the rest.
      Returns:
      the number of documents inserted

    • profileSchema

      public SchemaProfile profileSchema(String collection, int sampleSize)
      Samples up to sampleSize documents and profiles their shape — the schema analyser. Sampling uses $sample so it is spread across the collection rather than being the first page, which is what makes an optional field show up at all.

    • collectionStats

      public Map<String,String> collectionStats(String collection)
      Collection statistics for the details panel.

      Read with the $collStats aggregation stage on 6.2+, where the collStats command is deprecated and shared Atlas tiers refuse it outright; older servers get the command. If the preferred route fails the other one is tried, so a deployment that reports a version it does not honour still shows its numbers.
